I came to this clinic during one of the most difficult moments a pet owner can face to discuss euthanasia for my 13-year-old dog, who is suffering and can barely walk.

For transparency, dogs are weighed and evaluated first, and if they are over a certain weight, the cost increases. Euthanasia is not guaranteed and is at the veterinarian’s discretion, which I understand.

What made this experience extremely upsetting was the lack of compassion and professionalism shown. Despite clearly explaining my dog’s condition, I was repeatedly pressured to try medications after I had already said no. Dr. Sherman stated that my request for euthanasia was “out of convenience” and described it as controversial, which was incredibly hurtful given my dog’s age and declining quality of life.

Dr. Sherman mentioned that there was a list of other clinics that provide euthanasia services. However, when I asked the front desk for this list, they refused to provide it. Instead, staff discussed my situation openly at the front desk, within earshot. I heard staff members talking about my request and making judgmental comments implying that I had decided to put my dog down without trying anything.

One front desk staff member even suggested, in a dismissive tone, that I could surrender my dog to a shelter if I wanted him euthanized. Being spoken to this way while dealing with an elderly, suffering pet was completely inappropriate and deeply upsetting.

While Dr. Sherman ultimately declined to perform the euthanasia which I respect the way the situation was handled lacked empathy, privacy, and basic respect. No pet owner should be made to feel judged or shamed during such a painful decision.

The exam fee was $85. If you are seeking compassionate end-of-life care, I recommend looking elsewhere. I personally had a much better experience with Honor Pet.

I hope this clinic takes this feedback seriously and improves staff professionalism and empathy, especially during end-of-life situations.

DO NOT COME HERE -- Our dog passed away after surgery and inadequate post-care.

Our Border Collie, Sparky, had surgery here on Oct 20, 2025, performed by Dr. Christian Croquenois at Cahuenga Veterinary Hospital. We were told the procedure went well, but the post-surgery instructions from Dr. Croquenois and the assisting nurse, Kevin, were unclear and incomplete. We were told to give Sparky his antibiotics only if he was "willing to take them", and no one showed us how to properly administer them or warned us of the risks of delayed doses.

Because of this lack of guidance, Sparky went several days without antibiotics. His condition declined rapidly -- lethargy, vomiting, and visible distress. When we returned on Oct 24, Dr. Croquenois acknowledged Sparky's condition but offered no follow-up treatment and simply directed us to go elsewhere. There was no sense of responsibility from the team that had just operated on him. Sparky shortly passed away on Oct 27.

We understand complications happen, but what we experienced was a lack of guidance, lack of follow-up care, and lack of accountability. Sparky was my brother's emotional support animal and losing him like this has been traumatic.

We tried to reach out to discuss what happened but there was no response. At this point, all we can do is share our experience in hopes that it prevents another family from suffering the same confusion and heartbreak.

Please be cautious. Ask every question possible. Our trust in Dr. Christian Croquenois and this hospital cost us Sparky's life.

It took me a while to be able to write a review, but it deserves to be shared. My experience with this hospital is only for euthanasia services for my beloved dog.

My girl 12 year old girl Luna was quoted 6-9 months due to an inoperable tumor in her chest cavity. Suddenly, only about three months into this quoted time, there was an evening where she stood up and was disoriented, breathing heavy, unfocused - and I knew it was time. In a sheer panic mode, I was looking up emergency 24/7 hospitals since it was already 9pm on a Monday when this happened (back on 7/7).

We arrived at the hospital (which I will also add looks very nice both outside and inside) and my boyfriends family ran ahead inside to get assistance. She was a big girl, so a stretcher was needed. Everyone there handled her with such immense care. They got everything set up, and let me come back and have a moment with her while they administered all of the proper medications to help her sleep easy. I literally started crying because I saw someone even cut a small heart out with the medical tape to put on her wrist where the IV was - something as small as this really truly makes such a difference both in the moment and in processing the situation after the fact.

The vet lady was seriously so kind, softly letting me know what was going on and that she wasn't in any pain. They had a little room afterwards and brought her in so we could all have a moment to say our goodbyes - they even cut some of the specific ear fur from the spot I always pet her the most, and gave it to me before I left. Since she was a big girl, her euthanasia costs were about $600 but this also included the cremation costs. She came with a beautiful wooden box, a nose print with her name (i literally cried), another big bag of her fur and even an ornament with a paw print.

If you are for any reason looking into options for your beloved pet who will be crossing the bridge soon, or plan to at home but want a back up option in case something happens - I would recommend MASH. Thank you so much for making an already seriously sad and stressful situation so much easier, and doing it with such compassion.

The hospital I took him to admitted him immediately. These pictures were among the last ever taken of him. I will forever wonder what would have happened if the front office staff at DTLAvets had been more knowledgeable and more qualified to diagnose the signs of acute toxicity syndrome.

I do not recommend that you take your pet here for routine care. I do not recommend you take your pet here for emergency care. I do not recommend you take your pet here at all. I will forever think of the front office staff members laughing and talking amongst themselves as my boy was dying, and being completely ignored, and being callous and indifferent when I told them that I could tell that we could not continue to wait any longer.

Sometimes you have to trust your instincts. And my instincts are that the front office folks at DTLAvets will kill your pets with neglect and not think twice about it. And actually blame you for not being willing to wait your turn in line, as the doctor attends to routine cases while your pet is showing signs of neurological impairment.

--------------------------------------------

I recently had a disappointing experience at DTLAvets. Despite having an urgent care appointment for my dog, Pancake, we waited over thirty minutes while his condition worsened. The staff did not acknowledge the urgency of his situation, and the environment seemed to add to his distress.

To make matters worse, another dog in the waiting room was barking at Pancake, increasing his anxiety. When I asked if we could wait elsewhere, the staff refused and did not show any empathy for our situation. They did not make any effort to create a comfortable environment for animals in need of urgent care.

On a positive note, Dr. Coward is a very kind and gentle veterinarian. He has a wonderful demeanor, and Pancake always feels safe with him. I only wish the rest of the staff shared his empathy and compassion.

In the end, I had to take Pancake to another veterinarian who immediately recognized the seriousness of his condition and admitted him to the ICU. Pancake is now receiving treatment for suspected acute toxin exposure, a condition that DTLAvets failed to appropriately triage.

Overall, I am very disappointed with the lack of urgency and care shown by DTLAvets and would not recommend their services for pets in need of immediate attention.

On 10/26, he broke his dewclaw at the park. It was a minor injury, there was barely any bleeding. My regular vet couldn't get us in, so I made the mistake of going to Echo Park Veterinary Hospital for the first time.

My appointment was at 2:30 pm, right after their lunch break, and my first impression was that the vet appeared sleepy. The vet listened to San's heart and said he sounded "strong” and gave me the treatment plan. When I saw it, I repeatedly asked if anesthesia was necessary for a simple nail trim. The technician insisted it was. It is clear in hindsight that they just wanted to upcharge me for a simple procedure. They took him away, and that was the last time I ever saw San alive.

A while later, the vet came out and told me San was dead. The vet told me it was likely a "pulmonary embolism." This was a complete lie. They let me into the "operating room," and I was horrified. The place looked run-down, and San was on a ventilator, but there wasn't even a heart monitor in sight.

Later, I was given the medical notes, all written after the event with parts scratched out. The notes indicate they tried to give him two 0.5cc of dexmedetomidine and claimed one "missed”. Most importantly, the notes show no attempt to administer Antisedan, the reversal agent for dexmedetomidine.

My perfectly healthy dog died on their table from a broken nail. I am sharing our story so this doesn't happen to anyone else's family. Do not take your pet to this hospital.

I immediately put him back into the carrier and rushed him to my local vet, as ACCESS is an hour away. They were horrified to learn that a clinic had left Bobby leave in the condition they had to the point where they had me talk to the head nurse because she never wants to recommend patients to this surgery center again. Go elsewhere. I wish I had.

text.text:
This hospital is a gift to all fur babies. I feel so fortunate that I was referred to this hospital for my dog's emergency injury. She needed to be seen quickly by a surgeon as well as a cardiologist because of her heart murmur. The hospital was quick and careful with everything they did.

Dr. Mark Parlier is an amazing doctor and incredible surgeon. He was not only thorough, but exceptionally kind to both me and my dog. We were so fortunate to have him as her doctor. Although we were dealing with a scary laceration injury and a concerning heart murmur, Dr. Parlier was positive, honest, and methodical with his planning. I truly cannot thank him enough. Not only was he an excellent surgeon and was able to fully close her paw pad wounds to reduce the potential for infections and reduce the healing time process, he was also incredibly diligent with addressing her heart condition. I felt confident with his coordination with the cardiologist and that he was putting my dog's heart condition as the priority. He also took the time to discuss the progression of her heart disease with me and to discuss options for me to continue to care for her heart condition going forward. He was truly wonderful! When he came out of surgery to give me an update, he gave me a small thumbs up as he was walking toward me. It's those little things that make all the difference. I felt like I had barely been breathing during her surgery and that thumbs up allowed me to catch my breath finally. His follow up after surgery was detailed and understandable. At no point did I feel rushed and he allowed me the time to ask all of the questions I needed. Upon discharge, I felt fully informed and didn’t feel like I didn’t get to ask something necessary. I cannot express enough how exceptional Dr. Parlier is and how well he handled our situation. He is truly extraordinary! I am confident her situation would not have resulted in the same success had we not had him and VCA West Los Angeles to care for her.

I would recommend this hospital and staff to anyone I know for the best care for their animals. I feel so fortunate.

text.text:
All I can say is great things about this hospital  I in all honesty wouldn’t go anywhere else.

I have two elder dogs, and VCA Specialty Hospital has been an absolute blessing. One of my dogs had CHF, and the Cardiology Team gave me precious extra time with my soul animal through an LAD surgery (which isn’t performed in any other hospital) and their incredible ongoing care. They monitored him closely both before and after the surgery, adjusting his heart medications with precision and checking his organ levels weekly or twice a month to make sure he was always within a healthy range. Their attention to detail, compassion, and teamwork were truly extraordinary.

Dr. Garretto was not only brilliant and responsive always replying to my questions right away but he was also someone my boy truly loved. He was never afraid to go to his appointments. Every time we drove into the parking garage, he would lift his little head high, excited because he knew he was about to see his favorite person. That kind of trust says everything about the care and energy Dr. Garretto gives to his patients.

Dr. Barrett was another incredible part of our journey. She was always very honest with me, and I truly respected her for that even if it wasn’t what I wanted to hear. She offered extra alternatives and thoughtful options to help give me as much quality time as possible with my boy. Her thoroughness, compassion, and commitment over the year and a half we were under her care meant so much she was always fully present and truly cared.

Dr. Doan was also wonderful , often responding to my late-night emails (sometimes at 1 or 2 a.m.), bringing me reassurance and comfort during emotional times.

When it was time for my boy to pass, the entire staff showed so much empathy and love. They sent flowers, reached out personally, and Dr. Garretto gave us the most beautiful, memorable memorial gift 💝 one that I will cherish forever. These are the kinds of humans you want caring for your fur children  genuine, loving, and wholeheartedly dedicated  and I am endlessly grateful for them.

A special thank-you to Roxanne, the cardiology vet technician, who has been an incredible source of emotional support. She’s not only skilled but also so easy to talk to ,she helped me process the grief and still is currently.  I find comfort through her kindness and empathy.

My other dog has her own health issues that were caught early while I was caring for my boy, and we’re so lucky to have Dr. Otero on our team now to catch this early on. He is an exceptionally dedicated and highly skilled doctor , the best in the game! I’ve even received emails from him in the early mornings, checking in and offering guidance. He truly goes above and beyond to help. His compassion, depth of knowledge, and steady presence bring such peace of mind. He’s supported by his amazing staff Yessica and Ruth, who share that same level of care and professionalism. They even sent a sympathy card for my boy  who wasn’t their patient ,simply out of genuine kindness.

I’ve been coming to VCA for over a year and have never had a single issue  from anyone on the cardiology department to the primary care team , or front desk they all have been professional, thorough, kind, and full of heart, they all have gotten to know us & treat us like family .

I rarely write reviews, but this one felt necessary. This is my genuine testimony of gratitude for the VCA Specialty Hospital team — they are exceptional humans doing extraordinary work, and I’ll forever be thankful for the love, compassion, and care they’ve shown my fur family.

There are other emergency vets, I recommend going to another vet.
